title: A hyperglycemia–urine-creatinine interaction did not establish incremental cross-cohort urine-osmolality prediction
abstract: Urinary creatinine is a conventional dilution proxy but need not track all urinary osmoles. We tested one fixed interaction, log urine creatinine times serum glucose excess above 180 mg/dL, for predicting log measured urine osmolality beyond flexible separate urinary and routine serum measures. Source NHANES2009–2010 contained 5348 adults; frozen models were tested in 4577 separately recruited NHANES2011–2012 adults. MEC-weighted MSE changed from 0.076228 to 0.076369; gain was -0.000141 (500 source-refit/target-resample rescaled PSU-bootstrap95% interval -0.000408 to 0.000367). No incremental benefit was established. Subgroup and hinge-adjustment point estimates varied; they do not override the primary negative result. Transfer is across recruitment cohorts within one survey platform, not across clinical systems. This representation-specific test is not a hydration diagnosis, renal-threshold estimate or clinical-utility validation. Autonomous AI analysis and author self-checks; no new data collection.
